date: DRAFT, set to the day of the founder ruling
title: The PRD workspace calls the Claude API from edge functions with our own tool loop, not OpenRouter and not Managed Agents
decision: Every PRD model call (main, section and NGO side chats, the completion check, and the planning package's generations) goes to the Claude API from an edge function, with a server-held key in a platform PRD workspace, through the Discovery model port. Reserve the request's maximum cost before the call, price the reported token usage with versioned rates as paid Discovery does, and settle once per provider message identifier. Missing usage stays pending; a call rejected before generation releases its reservation; nightly reconciliation against the PRD workspace's provider report posts drift as a visible adjustment. Repository and Linear writes stay with the backend's own writers (REQ-026). OpenRouter leaves REQ-006, REQ-009, REQ-034 and REQ-036. Managed Agents is not adopted; revisit it for the planning package only if a package step cannot finish inside one edge function call or the package must run code against the repository.
evidence: loop/items/ai-path/memo.md. Measured in this run: the path-neutral ledger (hold before call, refusal on short funds, settle once, pending for missing cost, reconcile once, one winner of two parallel holds) on the local stack, and no key in the browser stream on all three paths in the Supabase edge runtime. Read: shipped paid Discovery metering (discovery_turn_reserve and discovery_turn_settle), Managed Agents session usage (list_cost rounded to cents and session-cumulative, runtime at 0.08 USD per active hour), the Anthropic cost report (daily, grouped by workspace), OpenRouter usage accounting, and the Supabase edge function limits (400 seconds wall clock on paid plans). Not measured: live streaming, tool calls, cost and latency, because the session had no provider keys.
supersedes: The OpenRouter clause of d93 and the OpenRouter wording that d99 kept in REQ-036.
